observations.body: Each household kills an unblemished animal, puts blood on the doorway, eats in haste, and is passed over when Egypt’s firstborn die.
observations.label: The Passover animal marks the houses

observations.body: The passage presents household animal, blood sign, meal, judgment, and deliverance as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: household animal, blood sign, meal, judgment, and deliverance

observations.body: The passage places passover sacrifice beside household animal, blood sign, meal, judgment, and deliverance.
observations.label: passover sacrifice

payload.posture: Read Exodus 12:1–32 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the blood marks Israelite houses; the passage does not call the animal a sin offering
